Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for Bangladesh's reply. The two umpires and players have made their way out to the middle. Shadman Islam and Zakir Hasan will open the innings for Bangladesh. Jasprit Bumrah will start with the red cherry for India. Let's play...
... THIRD INNINGS ...

Right then, based on our estimations, we have 19 overs left in the day, but it's doubtful we will get through all of them. However, play can be extended by an additional 30 minutes if the light permits, allowing for a total of 45 minutes of play remaining today. The Bangladesh openers face a tough task ahead in negotiating this tricky phase before the close of play, while India will be hoping for early inroads. Back in a bit.

Though Shubman Gill and Rishabh Pant fell in quick succession after Tea, Virat Kohli and KL Rahul ensured that the Indian innings did not lose momentum. After being given a couple of lives, Kohli fell just 3 runs short of his fifty, while Rahul continued to thrive. On their way to 285, India brought up the fastest team scores of 50, 100, 150, 200, and 250 in Test cricket history, eventually ending with a lead of 52 runs. For Bangladesh, Shakib Al Hasan and Mehidy Hasan contributed with four wickets each.

With the fall of the wicket, the declaration has come from Rohit Sharma! It was quite an eventful 34.4 overs, during which India scored 285 runs at a remarkable rate of 8.22. The innings began with Yashasvi Jaiswal and Rohit Sharma making their intentions clear as India raced to 50 runs in just 3 overs, the fastest by any team in Test cricket. This aggressive approach left Bangladesh stunned, unable to catch their breath as India maintained relentless momentum throughout their innings.

Commentary.Commentary: Drinks break! A much-needed pause, especially for Bangladesh, who have struggled to regain control. Their fielding has been subpar, allowing several chances to slip by. India, on the other hand, have kept the pressure on, adding 81 runs in the 10 overs since Tea and now trail by just 14 runs. Najmul Hossain Shanto and his team will need to regroup during this break to stop the haemorrhaging of runs. The next phase will be crucial, as all eyes will be on how India approach the game once they surpass Bangladesh's total. During the drinks break, the 12th man Yash Dayal came out with a message from Rohit Sharma for the two batters, likely outlining the strategy for the remainder of the session.

Commentary.Commentary: Welcome back for the third and final session of Day 4. This will be a 2-hour session, but we do have the option of extending play by an extra 30 minutes, provided the light permits. There are 40 overs left to be bowled in the day. Najmul Hossain Shanto and his men are in a huddle near the ropes before taking their respective positions on the field. Khaled Ahmed will kick things off with the ball. Khaled to Gill first up. Away we go...
... DAY 4, SESSION 3 ...

With minimal help from the pitch, Bangladesh will need to maintain tight lines and lengths to keep the runs in check. However, with India’s attacking approach, it seems unlikely they will back off. Instead, they might push harder to strengthen their position, making for an exciting final session. Join us again at 9.30 am GMT for the concluding part of the day's play!

India’s openers, Rohit Sharma and Yashasvi Jaiswal, came out attacking, breaking the record for the fastest team fifty in Test cricket, reaching the milestone in just 18 balls. Mehidy Hasan’s introduction of spin paid off, as he removed Rohit Sharma, preventing a missed review from hurting Bangladesh. Jaiswal continued his aggressive innings, reaching his half-century with solid support from Shubman Gill before falling to Hasan Mahmud just before Tea.

Bangladesh’s batting fell apart quickly after Lunch, as India stuck to their plan. Starting the session at 205/6, Bangladesh collapsed to 233 all out. Jasprit Bumrah was pivotal, removing Mehidy Hasan, which led to the quick dismissal of the remaining batters. Mominul Haque fought alone for Bangladesh, staying unbeaten on 107, but got little support from the rest of the lineup.

SESSION SUMMARY - 24.2 overs, 166 runs and 6 wickets. Despite losing both openers, India will be satisfied with their position at Tea on Day 4, sitting comfortably at 138/2 after just 16 overs and trailing by just 95 more runs. The Indian bowlers executed their plan flawlessly to wrap up Bangladesh earlier in the session, and their aggressive approach with the bat has given them control.

Commentary.Commentary: Starts from over the wicket and bowls it on a nagging length around middle and gets the ball to turn in, Yashasvi Jaiswal clips it through square leg for a single.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 4.1: Taijul Islam to Yashasvi Jaiswal, 1 run.

Commentary.Commentary: Taijul Islam is introduced into the attack and it will be spin from both ends.
Tosses it full, on middle and off, Shubman Gill prods out and pushes it back to the bowler.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.6: Mehidy Hasan to Shubman Gill, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Shubman Gill walks out to bat at number 3 for India!

OUT! CLEANED HIM UP! Mehidy Hasan eventually gets his man! So the decision not to review in the previous over has not cost much to Bangladesh. Hasan loops it up and slows it up a bit, full and turning in, around off, Rohit Sharma is a bit tentative to come on the front foot and smother the spin. The ball dips, grips and spins in sharply to beat Rohit on the inside edge. It sneaks through the gap between the bat and pad to crash into the stumps. Bangladesh get a much-needed breakthrough. Rohit goes for 23 (11). India are now 55/1, trailing by 178 runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.5: Mehidy Hasan to Rohit Sharma, OUT! b Mehidy Hasan.

Commentary.Commentary: Given LBW but successfully overturned by Rohit Sharma! Mehidy fires it in, short and on middle and leg, Rohit Sharma rocks back for the pull but he is late into the shot. Gets beaten on the inside edge and gets hit near the knee roll on the front pad. A loud shout and the finger is raised! Rohit Sharma has missed a straight delivery and looks to be a goner here. He has sent it upstairs though. Does he think it is going down leg? There is no bat involved but the Ball Tracking shows the impact to be outside leg, much to the delight of the Indian fans.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.4: Mehidy Hasan to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Pushed through quicker and fuller, down leg, Rohit Sharma tries to help it on the way but misses.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.3: Mehidy Hasan to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Digs it in short and on middle and leg, Rohit Sharma charges down the track but adjust well and tucks it to mid-wicket.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.2: Mehidy Hasan to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Smeared away! Floated up, full and on middle and leg, Rohit Sharma clears his front leg and swipes it up and over mid-wicket for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 3.1: Mehidy Hasan to Rohit Sharma, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Early signs of spin as Mehidy Hasan comes into the attack.

FOUR! Skillfully done! 22 runs off the over and that brings up India's 50 in just three overs. FASTEST FIFTY for a team in Test cricket, beating England's record of achieving the feat in 26 balls. Mahmud gets the yorker in, outside off, Yashasvi Jaiswal opens the bat face and glides it wide of deep third for four more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.6: Hasan Mahmud to Yashasvi Jaiswal, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! More runs! Mahmud goes into the deck and keeps it slower as well, on middle, Yashasvi Jaiswal adjusts well and rolls his wrists on the ball. Pulls it behind square on the leg side for a boundary.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.5: Hasan Mahmud to Yashasvi Jaiswal, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Yashasvi Jaiswal takes the aerial route now! Mahmud takes pace off and serves it full, outside off, Yashasvi Jaiswal opens up the off side and goes inside out over cover. Clears the fence with ease for a six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.4: Hasan Mahmud to Yashasvi Jaiswal, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: A direct hit! On a fullish length, on middle and leg, Yashasvi Jaiswal jams it out in front of mid on and Rohit Sharma sets off for a run. He gets sent back in time as the throw comes in from mid on. The fielder hits the stumps at the bowling end and it is referred upstairs but the replays show that Rohit was well in.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Hasan Mahmud to Yashasvi Jaiswal, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Oh dear! Mehidy Hasan's earlier caught-behind appeal on 2.1 proves to be justified as the UltraEdge shows a spike as the ball went under Rohit Sharma's bat. He survives, and that missed opportunity will surely haunt Bangladesh!
NO BALL! Low full toss, angling in, at the pads, Rohit Sharma flicks it to deep backward square leg for a single. Mahmud has overstepped.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.3: Hasan Mahmud to Rohit Sharma, No ball!

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! Monstrous! Mahmud sees the batter back away and tries to follow him but ends up serving it right in the arc, on middle and leg, Rohit Sharma clears his front leg and clobbers it over deep mid-wicket for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.2: Hasan Mahmud to Rohit Sharma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: A half-hearted appeal for caught behind but turned down! Mehidy Hasan standing at cover is pretty convinced and to be fair to him, there was a noise as the ball passed the bat. He does not get any support from the bowler or the keeper and Bangladesh do not take the review. Shaping away, on a good length, outside off, Rohit Sharma pokes at the delivery and gets beaten as the ball stays a bit low and goes under the bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 2.1: Hasan Mahmud to Rohit Sharma, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Streaky! Khaled angles it across the batter, on off, on a good length, the ball keeps a bit low. Yashasvi Jaiswal pushes at the delivery away from his body. Gets a bottom edge that races past the left of the man at first slip for a boundary. Just the lone slip and a gully were in place for this ball.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.6: Khaled Ahmed to Yashasvi Jaiswal, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: A slight hold in play as the umpires check the shape of the ball for the second time! Najmul Hossain Shanto doesn't seem to be happy with it but the ball goes through the ring and the umpire asks to carry on!
Fuller now by Ahmed, not much movement in the air or off the deck, on off, Yashasvi Jaiswal lunges and firms the drive to mid off.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.5: Khaled Ahmed to Yashasvi Jaiswal, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Beaten! More like it from Khaled! He hits the deck hard and gets a good lift off the deck, around the off-stump line, not wide enough for the cut. Yashasvi Jaiswal goes after it and gets beaten as the ball goes over his bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.4: Khaled Ahmed to Yashasvi Jaiswal, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Khaled sprays it down leg, on a length, Rohit Sharma lets it go. The keeper, Litton Das dives to his left and does well to get some glove on it. The ball gets parried away to his left for a bye.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.3: Khaled Ahmed to Rohit Sharma, Bye.

Commentary.Commentary: SIX! BANG! Two in two for the Indian skipper! Khalel goes short but does not get it high enough to trouble the batter, on off. Rohit Sharma swivels and nails the pull over deep square leg for a biggie.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.2: Khaled Ahmed to Rohit Sharma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: The ball has landed on the top of a shamiana in the ground!

SIX! No sighters needed for Rohit Sharma! Khaled serves it on a length from over the wicket, on middle, Rohit Sharma stays leg side of the ball and skips down the track. Swings through the line and tonks it over long on for a six.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 1.1: Khaled Ahmed to Rohit Sharma, Six!

Commentary.Commentary: It will be Khaled Ahmed to share the attack from the other end.
Mahmud changes his angle of attack as he comes from around the wicket and keeps it around the off stump line, on a length, Yashasvi Jaiswal lets the ball come to him and defends it on the off side.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.6: Hasan Mahmud to Yashasvi Jaiswal, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Make it three in a row! Mahmud errs again as he bowls it short and wide on off. Yashasvi Jaiswal latches onto it in a flash and cuts it past backward point for four more runs.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.5: Hasan Mahmud to Yashasvi Jaiswal, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! This is even better! Pitched up by Mahmud but a bit too full by Mahmud, on middle and leg, Yashasvi Jaiswal stays balanced in the crease and gets his bat out in front of the front pad. Drives it to the right of mid on for back-to-back boundaries.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.4: Hasan Mahmud to Yashasvi Jaiswal, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: FOUR! Yashasvi Jaiswal and ​​​​India are away! Width on offer by Mahmud, on a length, Yashasvi Jaiswal throws his hands at the delivery and cracks it through covers for the first boundary of the Indian innings.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.3: Hasan Mahmud to Yashasvi Jaiswal, Four!

Commentary.Commentary: Gets the shape again but the line is down leg, on a back of a length, Yashasvi Jaiswal gets inside the line to tickle it fine but misses. Good diving stop by the keeper, Litton Das low to his right.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.2: Hasan Mahmud to Yashasvi Jaiswal, No run.

Commentary.Commentary: Hasan steams in from over the wicket and gets a hint of inward shape, on a hard length, on off and middle, Yashasvi Jaiswal shuffles across and covers the line of the ball to keep it out with a straight bat.
Commentary.Default_Commentary: 0.1: Hasan Mahmud to Yashasvi Jaiswal, No run.
